source.title: How Learning Governs Unlearning across the Memorization-Generalization Spectrum
source.authors: Hwiyeong Lee; H. Lim; Ingyu Bang; Hoki Kim; Taeuk Kim

record.tranche_reason: The study reports training and test-accuracy results on modular addition and bucketed modular addition that bear on grokking, but the bucketed task is a modified setting and the study does not test whether the delay grows as the training set shrinks.
record.gate_note: The paper also reports extensive unlearning results, including retain accuracy and Fourier-circuit changes during unlearning. Those outcomes do not measure the training-time progress named by the claim versions, so they are not included as rows. The paper describes some training trajectories qualitatively and supplies endpoint accuracies; it does not report a training-set-size sweep.
record.test_reason: Grokking is mainly a tool here: it separates memorizing from generalizing models before unlearning. The study does add one result of its own. It introduces a new variant, bucketed modular addition (BMA), and reports for M ≤ 64 that 'test bucket accuracy rises long after training exact accuracy saturates' (Fig. 3, §4.2). That bears on V1 in a modified algorithmic setting. The plain modular-addition run copies an original source's (Nanda et al.) setup and reports only selected checkpoints, so it adds no independent test.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is mostly right but misplaces the emphasis. The authors' main conclusion is that retain damage in unlearning grows with a model's reliance on shared generalizing mechanisms rather than memorization. They show this in modular addition (grokked models are damaged more), across BMA bucket sizes (nearly monotonic), and in Hubble LLMs for verbatim and factual recall. Grokking serves only as the lens for building memorizing and generalizing models.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses one-layer transformers, modular addition, and a 30% training split, and reports training/test accuracy at checkpoints or across BMA bucket sizes. The BMA task adds randomized within-bucket labels; the paper does not sweep training-set size.
record.method_sensitivity: BMA bucket size changes the share of answer information determined by the modular rule; the paper does not vary training-set size to test its effect on grokking delay.
record.problems: For the original modular-addition checkpoints, the paper gives only a range of test accuracy across four checkpoints, not checkpoint-specific values or the timing of the test-accuracy rise. For BMA, it describes the delayed rise qualitatively and reports endpoint test accuracies, but does not quantify the delay. The training-set-size dependence in V1 is not tested.
record.rows_left_out: Unlearning outcomes, including retain accuracy, Fourier variance explained, restricted loss, and circuit-filtering interventions (§3 and Appendices B.3–B.4), are left out because they measure behavior during unlearning rather than the training-time grokking behavior in the claim versions.

untested.parts: Whether the delay grows as the training set shrinks: only a 30% split is used, with no size sweep. The size of the delay is also never quantified.
Gradual circuit formation and progress measures anticipating the jump. FVE is shown at training checkpoints only as a baseline for unlearning.
All untested. The Hubble LLMs are studied only for unlearning.
All untested. Weight decay is fixed at 1.

record.verdict_notes: Figure 2 shows the Fourier-circuit FVE at four training checkpoints before unlearning: low at memorization, 0.97 when grokked. This loosely echoes V2 but does not test whether progress measures anticipate the jump, and the intermediate values are given only in the figure. Within-bucket accuracy stays at chance, so the delayed rise concerns only the rule-determined part of the answer. The study is a preprint.

versions.untested_parts: Whether the delay grows as the training set shrinks.

The study does not measure gradual formation of the generalizing circuit during training, later removal of memorizing components, or whether continuous progress measures anticipate a test-accuracy jump. Its circuit measurements concern changes during unlearning.
Non-algorithmic data and initialization-scale or weight-norm changes inducing a lazy-to-rich transition.
Delayed generalization during realistic LLM pretraining or fine-tuning.
Whether low-norm bias selects a more efficient circuit, and whether there is a critical dataset size or ungrokking below it.
Whether independent runs converge to the same identifiable algorithm across architectures and hyperparameters.
Whether grokking delays are artifacts of adaptive optimizers or floating-point limits in the softmax.

rows.subject: one-layer transformer, modular addition (p = 113)
rows.operation_detail: Measured training and test accuracy at four checkpoints spanning memorization, circuit formation, cleanup, and the grokked regime.
rows.value: All four checkpoints had 100% training accuracy; test accuracy ranged from poor generalization to 100%.
rows.note: The text reports the range across the four selected checkpoints but does not give each checkpoint's test accuracy or quantify the delay before test accuracy improves.
rows.check: These are checkpoint-selection values from a single run that replicates the original source's (Nanda et al.) configuration. The text gives only 'poor generalization to 100%' across hand-picked checkpoints, with no trajectory or delay. That is a selection description, not a result on V1.

relation.reason: Training and held-out bucket-accuracy trajectories directly bear on V1 in the BMA setting.

tranche.reason: The new bucketed modular-addition setting reports its own delayed-generalization trajectories, beyond using grokking to study unlearning.

source_check.notes: The generalizing metric is bucket accuracy; within-bucket selection remains near chance. Delay is qualitative, and the study does not test how delay changes with training-set size.

statements.correction: BMA: 100% training accuracy; test bucket accuracy rises much later. Explicit endpoints: M = 4, 93.57%; M = 16, 93.82%; M = 64, 96.63%. M = 1: approaches 1, exact endpoint unstated. One-layer transformer; 30% training split; AdamW weight decay 1; delay unquantified.
BMA has p = 256/M buckets; chance bucket accuracy is M/256: 1/256 at M = 1 and 1/4 at M = 64. These fractions follow from the task definition; Figure 3 marks chance levels.
